title: 1988 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Let \(f(x)=4x-x^2.\) Given \(x_0,\) consider the sequence defined by \(x_n=f(x_{n-1})\) for all \(n\ge1.\) For how many real numbers \(x_0\) will the sequence \(x_0,\) \(x_1,\) \(x_2,\) \(\ldots\) take on only a finite number of different values?

solutions.text:
The starting values \(0,4,2\) give finite orbits \(0\), \(4\to0\), and \(2\to4\to0.\) More generally, if \(a_n\) begins a finite chain ending at \(0,\) solve \[ 4a_{n+1}-a_{n+1}^2=a_n. \] Its real solutions are \(a_{n+1}=2\pm\sqrt{4-a_n}.\) Choosing a preimage not already in the chain extends it by one new value. Repeating produces infinitely many distinct starting values with finite orbits.

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Start with \(0,\) then find numbers mapping successively to \(0\)
For every \(a\le4,\) solve \(4x-x^2=a\) and choose a new real preimage
